extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) preparing or responding to Office actions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and form-paragraph criteria for drafting and analyzing Office action rejections and objections under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102, 103, 112 (pre- and post-AIA), and related procedural rules. Covers when to use specific form paragraphs, statutory bases, and common examiner practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) for common ownership/joint research
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) establishing that, not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention, the subject matter disclosed and the claimed invention were either owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person or subject to a joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph only in applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 (AIA); must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia. Use to reject over a reference with an earlier effective filing date that ONLY qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2). Do NOT use if the reference qualifies under 102(a)(1) (use form paragraph 7.21.aia instead). Insert explanation in bracket 4 as needed. See MPEP §717.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) — common assignee/applicant/joint inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as obvious over a reference that has a common assignee, common applicant (35 U.S.C. 118), or at least one common joint inventor and which constitutes prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) by virtue of an earlier effective U.S. filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection might be overcome by: (1) a 37 CFR 1.132 showing derivation of the reference's subject matter from this application's inventor; (2) showing an earlier date of invention under 37 CFR 1.131(a); or (3) an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(c) that current ownership is common and that the named inventor is the prior inventor under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 104 plus a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(c). Also consider disqualification under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c). Follow MPEP §§706.02(l)(1)-(3). Fill bracket placeholders: claim numbers, prior art reference, and which common relationship (assignee/applicant/joint inventor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection — 35 U.S.C. 103, 'further in view of' (combination of references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as unpatentable over a primary reference as applied to another claim and further in view of an additional reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For AIA applications (filed on/after March 16, 2013), use only when claims are examined under AIA 102/103 and must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia and 7.21.aia. An explanation of the rejection must follow (see MPEP §2144). For pre-AIA use form paragraph 7.22.fti and ensure proper determination of any 102(e) date per MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graham v. Deere factual inquiries for obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: The factual inquiries applied to determine obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103: (1) determine the scope and content of the prior art; (2) ascertain the differences between the prior art and the claims at issue; (3) resolve the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art; (4) consider objective evidence (secondary considerations) indicating obviousness or nonobviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph when appropriate, e.g., in response to arguments regarding applicability of Graham v. John Deere factors. Applicable both AIA and pre-AIA contexts; must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia for AIA files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of combined 35 U.S.C. 102/103 form paragraph (7.27) — when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102([paragraph]) as anticipated by or, alternatively, under 35 U.S.C. 103 as obvious over a cited reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This combined paragraph is NOT intended as a common substitute for making a single clear rejection under 102 or 103; use only in special circumstances such as: disputed claim interpretation leading to either 102 or 103; where the reference discloses all limitations except a property/function with uncertainty about inherent properties (In re Fitzgerald); genus/species issues (In re Schaumann); product-by-process concerns (In re Marosi); means-plus-function equivalence uncertainty; overlapping ranges without a specific example in reference. If used, must be preceded by specified form paragraphs (e.g., 7.07.aia, 7.08.aia, 7.12.aia) and must be followed by a full explanation of both anticipation and obviousness grounds. For priority claims predating March 16, 2013, precede with form paragraph 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection — New Matter Added to Specification (35 U.S.C. 132(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment is objected to under 35 U.S.C. 132(a) because it introduces new matter into the disclosure; the added material not supported by the original disclosure must be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must cancel the new matter in reply. Do not use for reissue applications (use 14.22.01). In bracket 2 identify new matter by page/lines or figures and provide an explanation addressing any applicant statements claiming support. If new matter affects claims, also make a 35 U.S.C. 112(a) / first paragraph rejection (form paragraph 7.31.01). Include a full explanation following this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure/Claims Objected to — Minor Informalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure or claims are objected to because of minor informalities (spelling errors, inconsistent terminology, numbering issues, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to point out minor corrections required; cite specific informalities in bracket placeholders. See form paragraphs 6.28–6.31 for examples. If informalities render claims indefinite, use the appropriate 112 rejection (7.34.01). Precedence rules for form paragraphs apply (e.g., must be preceded by 7.07.fti and others as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Objected — Reference Characters Not Enclosed Within Parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims objected to because reference characters corresponding to elements in the detailed description/drawings are not enclosed within parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference characters in claims should be enclosed in parentheses to avoid confusion with other numbers/characters. If lack of parentheses renders claim(s) indefinite, use form paragraph 7.34.01 (112(b)). Cite MPEP §608.01(m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Objected — Spacing of Lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims objected to because lines are crowded too closely together, making reading difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require substitute claims with 1.5 or double spacing on good quality paper per 37 CFR 1.52(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure Objected — Embedded Hyperlinks or Browser-Executable Code
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure is objected to because it contains an embedded hyperlink and/or other form of browser-executable code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must delete embedded hyperlinks/browser-executable code; references to websites should be limited to top-level domain names without prefixes like 'http://'. Exceptions: nucleotide/amino acid sequence data between '< >' are not hyperlinks; electronic documents listed on PTO-892 and PTO/SB/08B may identify a URL. If incorporation by reference to hyperlinked content is attempted, use form paragraph 6.19 or 6.19.01. Do not object where hyperlinks themselves are necessary to meet 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and applicant intends them inactive — examiner should not object in that case. See MPEP §608.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Statutory Basis — 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (written description/enablement/best mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotations of 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (first paragraph) regarding written description, enablement and best mode requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory quotations are required only in first actions on the merits and final rejections (otherwise use form paragraph 7.103). Form paragraphs 7.30.01 and 7.30.02 must be used only once in a given Office action. Use appropriate follow-on form paragraphs (e.g., 7.31.xx) for specific defects (written description, enablement, best mode).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Statutory Basis — 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (definiteness/claiming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation of 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (second paragraph) requiring claims to particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in first actions on the merits and final rejections only (or use 7.103 otherwise). Use 7.30.02 only once per Office action. Follow with form paragraphs addressing particular deficiencies (7.34.xx).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Statutory Basis — 35 U.S.C. 112(f) / means-plus-function
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation of 35 U.S.C. 112(f) (sixth paragraph pre-AIA) regarding means or step-for claiming and construction to corresponding structure, material, or acts and equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only once per Office action when claim elements use 'means'/'step for' or otherwise invoke 112(f). Must be followed by form paragraph 7.30.04. The absence of the word 'means' raises a rebuttable presumption that 112(f) is not invoked; presence raises a presumption that it is invoked unless rebutted by clear claim structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Interpretation — presumptions regarding 'means' / 'step for'
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim elements using 'means' (or 'step for') are presumed to invoke 35 U.S.C. 112(f); elements not using 'means' are presumed not to invoke 112(f). The presumption is rebuttable when claim language supplies sufficient structure/material/acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph only once in an Office action when appropriate. Provide explanation when presumptions are rebutted (e.g., 'means' used but definite structure recited, or no 'means' but lacking structure). May be followed by specific 112-related form paragraphs (7.34.11, 7.34.16, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) — Written Description (possession)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (first paragraph) for failing the written description requirement: the claim contains subject matter not described in the specification in such a way as to reasonably convey to one skilled in the art that the inventor had possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify by reference (page/lines/figures) the missing support in bracket 2 and explain why the specification fails to convey possession; may precede form paragraph 7.30.03. Include any unresolved examiner questions and specific rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'Means' (7.30.04) — rebuttable presumption guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the word 'means' (or 'step for') with functional language creates a rebuttable presumption that the element is to be treated under 35 U.S.C. 112(f). The presumption is rebutted when the function is recited with sufficient structure, material, or acts within the claim itself to entirely perform the recited function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by 7.30.01 or 7.103. In bracket 2 identify any subject matter not properly described and explain why. Follow-up with appropriate 112(f)-related form paragraphs if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) — Enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) first paragraph for failing to enable one skilled in the art to make and/or use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 identify the claimed subject matter not enabled (by page/line or figures) and explain why, referencing unresolved examiner questions that raise doubt as to enablement. Apply In re Wands factors and MPEP §§2164 et seq. Precede with 7.30.01 or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) — Best Mode Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected because the best mode contemplated by the inventor (or joint inventor) has not been disclosed, with evidence of concealment identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rarely. Must be preceded by 7.30.01 or 7.103. In bracket 2 insert the basis for holding that best mode has been concealed (e.g., poor disclosure quality). If the problem is one of claim scope rather than best mode, consider 7.31.03 instead. Follow MPEP §§2165–2165.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection — Scope of Enablement (claims broader than enabled disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected because the specification, while enabling for some subject matter, does not reasonably provide enablement for other claimed aspects; the claims are not commensurate in scope with the enabling disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when claim scope exceeds what the specification enables. Identify enabling portions (bracket 2), aspects not enabled (bracket 3), whether enablement to 'make'/'use'/'make and use' is lacking (bracket 4), and the claimed subject matter not enabled (bracket 5). Apply Wands factors and provide detailed explanation (MPEP §§2164.01(a), 2164.04). Precede with 7.30.01 or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection 7.33.01 — Essential subject matter missing from claims (enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected because the disclosure does not enable one of ordinary skill to practice the invention without critical or essential subject matter that is omitted from the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 recite the omitted subject matter; in bracket 3 provide rationale for considering it critical/essential. Cite statements, arguments, dates, drawings, or other evidence showing applicant considered the feature essential. Precede with 7.30.01 or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) — Failure to claim inventor's invention (statement by applicant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected where inventor/applicant has stated somewhere outside the application as filed (e.g., remarks, brief, affidavit) that the invention is something different from what is defined in the claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only where such statements exist. Identify the submission by date (bracket 3), set forth what inventor/applicant stated (bracket 4), and explain how that statement indicates a different invention (bracket 5). Must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) — Indefiniteness (failure to particularly point out and distinctly claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected as indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103. Follow with one or more of form paragraphs 7.34.02–7.34.11 as applicable; if none apply, supply a full explanation identifying the term(s)/limitations rendering the claim indefinite and why, referencing MPEP §§2171–2174. For pro se applicants, consider 7.34.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology used inconsistent with accepted meaning (claim term redefinition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant acts as his/her own lexicographer to redefine a claim term contrary to its ordinary meaning, the written description must clearly redefine the term and put one skilled in the art on notice of the uncommon definition; otherwise the term is indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out applicant's claimed meaning (bracket 3) and the accepted meaning supported by citations (bracket 4). Use only where the specification does not clearly redefine the term. Precede with 7.34.01. Provide supporting reference (textbook/dictionary) per MPEP §2173.05(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative term/term of degree rendering claim indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: A relative term (term of degree) in a claim renders the claim indefinite where the claim/specification does not provide a standard for ascertaining the requisite degree and one of ordinary skill in the art would not be reasonably apprised of the scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the relative term (bracket 1) and the claim (bracket 2); explain why no ascertainable standard exists (bracket 3). Precede with 7.34.01 and follow MPEP guidance on terms of degree and definiteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of 102(e) prior art date for patents from international applications (AIPA / pre-AIPA rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for applying pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as amended by the American Inventors Protection Act (AIPA) and the pre-AIPA regime when references are U.S. patents issued from international (PCT) applications — treatment depends on international filing date relative to November 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reference is a U.S. patent or publication of a U.S. application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), or a U.S. patent issued from/ publication of an international application with international filing date on/after Nov 29, 2000, apply pre-AIA 102(e) as amended by AIPA. If reference issues from an international application filed prior to Nov 29, 2000, apply pre-AIPA 102(e). For continuing/national stage scenarios (35 U.S.C. 371, 120, 121, 365(c), 386(c)), follow MPEP guidance and the Examiner Notes for form paragraphs 7.12.fti and 7.12.01.fti to determine the correct date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph sequencing and prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Many form paragraphs require that specific other form paragraphs precede them in an Office action (e.g., 7.03.aia must precede certain AIA paragraphs; 7.30.01/7.30.02 used only once; 7.30.03 must be followed by 7.30.04 where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stated precedence for each form paragraph. Examples: use 7.03.aia before AIA-specific rejections; use 7.21.aia or 7.21.fti as prerequisites for 7.22; use 7.30.01/7.30.02 only once per action; 7.30.03 must be followed by 7.30.04. Ensure any form paragraph that cites a statute is used in the appropriate type of Office action (first action on the merits, final rejection) or substitute 7.103 when statute citation is omitted.
